'''Kajali''' is a dialect of the [[Tati language (Iran)|Tati language]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/kaja1247|title=Kajali|access-date=1 December 2025|website=Glottolog}}</ref> spoken in the village of [[Kajal, Iran|Kajal]] and a few surrounding villages around, in [[Ardabil province]], northwestern [[Iran]]. It is a [[Moribund language|moribund]] [[Northwestern Iranian languages|Northwestern Iranian language]] closely related to [[Talysh language|Talysh]]. The language, which has a small number of remaining speakers, has been replaced by Azerbaijani. Unlike the Azeris, the dominant community in the region, its speakers are Sunni Muslims.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|title=The Tāti Dialect of Kajal|last=Yarshater|first=Ehsan|date=1960|journal=Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies|issue=2|volume=23|pages=275, 276, 279}}</ref>

== Grammar ==
Similar to many other [[Tati language (Iran)|Tati]] dialects and closely related [[Zaza language|Zaza]], the Kajali dialect has a grammatical gender system based on the distinction between ''masculine'' and ''feminine''. The grammatical distinction between masculine and feminine is found in the conjugation of verbs as well as nouns.<ref name=":182">{{Cite journal |last=سبزعلیپور|first=جهاندوست|date=2013|title=تمایز جنس مونث و مذکر در گویش تاتی خلخال|trans-title=Distiniction of the Feminine and Masculine Gender in the Tāti Dialect of Khalkhāl|journal=نامه فرهنگستان|language=fa|volume=13|issue=1|pages=72, 74, 81}}</ref> In addition to grammatical gender, there are two grammatical cases, ''nominative'' and ''oblique'' in the dialect.<ref name=":0" />
